items.claim: The disclosed B-colon verb-ellipsis and the backslider-of-heart crux both hold against the pointed bytes, and the 13:1-13:2 comparison is correctly kept out of boundary_evidence_refs as non-adjacent, lexeme-free kinship.
items.evidence: Prov.14.14 byte text מִדְּרָכָ֣יו יִ֭שְׂבַּע ס֣וּג לֵ֑ב וּ֝מֵעָלָ֗יו אִ֣ישׁ טֽוֹב shows the B-colon (u-me'alav ish tov) has no finite verb of its own, confirming the row's claim that it borrows the A-colon's finite verb (yisba) by ellipsis rather than repeating it; no Hebrew lexeme is shared with 13:1-13:2, matching the row's own disclosure that the kinship claimed there is structural (ellipsis pattern), not lexical.

items.claim: The 'man of schemes' recurrence claim at 12:2 is byte-accurate at the exact digit cited and is correctly disclosed as non-adjacent, book-vocabulary reuse rather than a chaining link.
items.evidence: A skeleton-tier sweep of the two-word construction underlying וְאִ֥ישׁ מְ֝זִמּ֗וֹת (Prov.14.17) returns exactly 2 verses book-wide: Prov.12.2 (byte form וְאִ֖ישׁ מְזִמּ֣וֹת) and Prov.14.17 (byte form וְאִ֥ישׁ מְ֝זִמּ֗וֹת) -- matching the row's cited 'sweep: 2' precisely, with no further hits eluded by pointing or prefix variation. Prov.14.17 full byte text קְֽצַר אַ֭פַּיִם יַעֲשֶׂ֣ה אִוֶּ֑לֶת וְאִ֥ישׁ מְ֝זִמּ֗וֹת יִשָּׂנֵֽא confirms the adversative-waw pivot the row describes opening the B-colon on this shared phrase.

items.claim: The inherit/crown verb-pair reading and the disclosed waw-adversative pivot both match the pointed bytes without overclaim.
items.evidence: Prov.14.18 byte text נָחֲל֣וּ פְתָאיִ֣ם אִוֶּ֑לֶת וַֽ֝עֲרוּמִ֗ים יַכְתִּ֥רוּ דָֽעַת shows the inherit-root verb opening the A-colon and the crown-root verb opening the B-colon after a prefixed waw, exactly as the row's device_notes describe (folly and knowledge framed as things received rather than done); no digit-bearing or universal claim is made that needs a book-wide sweep.

items.claim: The synonymous-restatement reading (one subordination scene in two vocabularies) is defensible against the bytes and is correctly distinguished from the chapter's adversative-waw antithetic pattern.
items.evidence: Prov.14.19 byte text שַׁח֣וּ רָ֭עִים לִפְנֵ֣י טוֹבִ֑ים וּ֝רְשָׁעִ֗ים עַֽל שַׁעֲרֵ֥י צַדִּֽיק pairs two distinct lexeme-sets for evildoers/good-people across the two cola under a plain conjunctive waw, not the adversative-waw pivot that opens 14:17, 14:18, and 14:20-14:21 -- a real, byte-visible difference in the connector that supports classifying this verse as synonymous restatement rather than antithesis.

items.claim: The span touches an undisclosed ketiv/qere note at 14:21 inside the very clause the row glosses, and the row's 'to his neighbor' phrase claim blends two distinct shared objects without separating them.
items.evidence: pmarks_Prov.json's kq inventory carries exactly one Prov ch.14 note, at Prov.14.21 (single-witness, WLC); the byte text confirms an inline ketiv/qere pair עניים עֲנָוִ֣ים (unpointed ketiv followed by the pointed qere) sitting inside the clause the row glosses as 'gracious to the needy' -- left undisclosed in the row's prose although the note falls inside the row's own span. Separately, the row's cited catchword digit is accurate as a bare-word count (skeleton sweep of the word underlying לְ֭רֵעֵהוּ/Prov.14.20 returns 3 verses book-wide: Prov.11.12, Prov.14.20, Prov.14.21) but blends two different shared objects under one 'phrase' label: 14:20 and 14:21 share only that single word, while 14:21's actual verse-opening two-word construction בָּז לְרֵעֵ֥הוּ is skeleton-identical to Prov.11.12's opening בָּז לְרֵעֵ֥הוּ (sweep of that two-word construction: 2 verses book-wide, Prov.11.12 and Prov.14.21 only) -- a sharper, more specific link than the row's undifferentiated phrase framing discloses.

items.claim: The row's central cohesion claim -- that 14:26 and 14:27 open with 'the same two-word construct phrase... functioning as the same grammatical subject' -- is byte-false: 14:26's opening word carries a prefixed preposition 14:27 lacks, which changes both the word and its syntactic role.
items.evidence: consonantal_index.json skeleton for Prov.14.26 opens on the token ביראת (bet-prefixed), while Prov.14.27 opens on יראת (bare) -- these are two different words at the word-bound skeleton tier, not an identical opening phrase; a naive contiguous-substring sweep for the bare form nets 15 verses book-wide but wrongly counts 14:26 among them only because the bare string sits inside the longer prefixed token, the prefix-extension trap. The pointed bytes confirm the syntactic consequence: Prov.14.26 בְּיִרְאַ֣ת יְ֭הוָה מִבְטַח עֹ֑ז וּ֝לְבָנָ֗יו יִהְיֶ֥ה מַחְסֶֽה reads 'in the fear of YHWH [is] strong confidence,' where the fear-of-YHWH phrase (opening word בְּיִרְאַ֣ת) is a prepositional/adverbial modifier and the grammatical subject is the following noun phrase (strong confidence); Prov.14.27 יִרְאַ֣ת יְ֭הוָה מְק֣וֹר חַיִּ֑ים לָ֝ס֗וּר מִמֹּ֥קְשֵׁי מָֽוֶת reads 'the fear of YHWH [is] a fountain of life,' where the bare fear-of-YHWH phrase (opening word יִרְאַ֣ת) is itself the subject. The row uses the claimed identical-subject phrase to rank this pair's cohesion above the writer part's other catchword pairs, so the error is load-bearing for the cluster decision, not decorative.

items.claim: The two distinct body/breath-idiom temperament pair and the disclosed waw-adversative pivot both hold against the pointed bytes without overclaim.
items.evidence: Prov.14.29 byte text אֶ֣רֶךְ אַ֭פַּיִם רַב תְּבוּנָ֑ה וּקְצַר ר֝֗וּחַ מֵרִ֥ים אִוֶּֽלֶת carries two separate idioms (a nostril-length idiom for patience in the A-colon, a spirit/breath-shortness idiom for temper in the B-colon) rather than a shared noun, with the B-colon's turn carried by a prefixed waw, exactly as the row's device_notes describe; no digit-bearing or universal claim requiring a sweep is made.

items.claim: The row's disclosed crux -- that the B-colon's closing verb lacks a negative particle in the staged pointed text -- is byte-accurate, and declining to conjecturally supply one is the correct discipline.
items.evidence: Prov.14.33 byte text בְּלֵ֣ב נָ֭בוֹן תָּנ֣וּחַ חָכְמָ֑ה וּבְקֶ֥רֶב כְּ֝סִילִ֗ים תִּוָּדֵֽעַ carries no negative particle before the B-colon's closing verb, confirming the row's disclosure at face value; treating this as an observed textual crux rather than silently emending toward the chapter's usual antithetic pattern is disciplined given the staged extract carries no comparative/versional apparatus to adjudicate it.
